speaker: Unknown
en: Global hiring is such a headache when you're building fast, but companies like Eleven Labs are scaling effortlessly with Deal.
zh: 当你在快速构建时,全球招聘真是件头疼的事,但像 Eleven Labs 这样的公司正借助 Deal 轻松扩张。

speaker: Unknown
en: They quadrupled their workforce in 2025 without hiring an HR team.
zh: 它们在 2025 年让员工人数翻了两番,却没有组建一个人力资源团队。

speaker: Unknown
en: Build your global team with Deal.
zh: 用 Deal 打造你的全球团队。

speaker: Unknown
en: Visit deal.com slash MOS and start expanding your business today.
zh: 访问 deal.com/MOS,今天就开始拓展你的业务。

speaker: Unknown
en: That's D-E-E-L dot com slash MOS.
zh: 那是 D-E-E-L 点 com 斜杠 MOS。

speaker: Unknown
en: The future of work is arriving, and it's arriving on our shores right now, right here, whether we want it to or not.
zh: 工作的未来正在到来,而且不管我们愿不愿意,它此刻就在我们的海岸边到来,就在这里。

speaker: Unknown
en: The urgency and the need for all of us to become, you know, fluent in using AI for our jobs, I mean, that is something none of us can escape.
zh: 我们所有人都有紧迫感和必要去熟练地把 AI 用到工作中,我的意思是,这是谁也逃不掉的。

speaker: Unknown
en: You can't learn to ride a bike in a seminar.
zh: 你不可能在研讨会上学会骑自行车。

speaker: Unknown
en: And I think the same is true for AI.
zh: 我认为对 AI 来说也是同样的道理。

speaker: Unknown
en: Until you're using these tools day in and day out, you know, really integrating and pushing what's the boundaries of what they can do, that's when I think people become extremely capable.
zh: 直到你日复一日地使用这些工具,真正去整合它们、去推动它们能力的边界,那时我认为人们才会变得极其能干。

speaker: Unknown
en: Will humans win or machines win?
zh: 人类会赢还是机器会赢?

speaker: Unknown
en: I think that is distracting us from, in some cases, putting our collective societal energy towards building a future where everyone wins.
zh: 我认为这正在分散我们的注意力,让我们在某些情况下无法把整个社会的集体精力投入到建设一个人人皆赢的未来。

speaker: Unknown
en: That's Hayden Brown, CEO of Upwork, the global tech platform for freelance workers.
zh: 这位是 Hayden Brown,全球自由职业者技术平台 Upwork 的 CEO。

speaker: Unknown
en: As AI radically resets expectations across the workforce, Upwork has a critical vantage point on how the job market is actually evolving.
zh: 随着 AI 彻底重置整个劳动力的预期,Upwork 在就业市场如何真实演变上拥有一个关键的观察视角。

speaker: Unknown
en: I wanted to talk to Hayden about the on-the-ground reality beyond government job numbers and the dreamy predictions of AI cheerleaders.
zh: 我想和 Hayden 聊聊政府就业数据以及 AI 鼓吹者那些美梦般的预测之外的一线现实。

speaker: Unknown
en: Hayden is forthright about the pressures facing organizations and their teams, including her own decision to lay off Upwork staffers earlier this year.
zh: Hayden 坦率地谈到了组织及其团队所面临的压力,包括她自己今年早些时候裁减 Upwork 员工的决定。

speaker: Unknown
en: She shares which jobs are most in demand.
zh: 她分享哪些工作需求最大。

speaker: Unknown
en: The good and bad of AI agents and where she sees the future of work moving.
zh: AI 智能体的利与弊,以及她认为工作的未来将走向何方。

speaker: Unknown
en: Plus, she talks about the challenges of leading when even a one-year planning horizon is too far, revealing her specific practices for resetting strategy on the fly.
zh: 此外,她还谈到当连一年的规划周期都显得太远时,领导的挑战,并揭示了她随时重置战略的具体做法。

speaker: Unknown
en: So let's get to it.
zh: 那么让我们开始吧。

speaker: Unknown
en: I'm Bob Safian, and this is Rapid Response.
zh: 我是 Bob Safian,这里是 Rapid Response。

speaker: Unknown
en: I'm Bob Safian.
zh: 我是 Bob Safian。

speaker: Unknown
en: I'm here with Hayden Brown, president and CEO of Upwork.
zh: 我身边这位是 Upwork 的总裁兼 CEO Hayden Brown。

speaker: Unknown
en: Hayden, great to see you.
zh: Hayden,很高兴见到你。

speaker: Unknown
en: Great to see you, Bob.
zh: 很高兴见到你,Bob。

speaker: Unknown
en: Thanks for having me.
zh: 谢谢你邀请我。

speaker: Unknown
en: You were last a guest on the show.
zh: 你上次做客这个节目。

speaker: Unknown
en: We were talking geopolitics, Russia, Ukraine.
zh: 我们当时聊的是地缘政治、俄罗斯、乌克兰。

speaker: Unknown
en: It was pre-Great Resignation, pre-return to office controversies, pre-Gaza and Iran.
zh: 那是在「大辞职」之前,在重返办公室争议之前,在加沙和伊朗之前。

speaker: Unknown
en: Now, of course, AI anxiety dominates workforce discussions.
zh: 而现在,当然,AI 焦虑主导着关于劳动力的讨论。

speaker: Unknown
en: It's like we've been through decades of change all piled together.
zh: 就好像我们把几十年的变化全堆积在一起经历了。

speaker: Unknown
en: How are you doing?
zh: 你最近怎么样?

speaker: Unknown
en: I mean, it's been a challenging time to be a CEO.
zh: 我的意思是,这是一个当 CEO 很有挑战的时期。

speaker: Unknown
en: You know, it definitely feels like there's a lot happening.
zh: 你知道,确实感觉有很多事情在发生。

speaker: Unknown
en: I have a kind of running joke with some friends who run other companies.
zh: 我和一些运营其他公司的朋友之间有个常讲的玩笑。

speaker: Unknown
en: We all say, you know, what's going to be the black swan event of this quarter?
zh: 我们都会说,你知道,这个季度的黑天鹅事件会是什么?

speaker: Unknown
en: Because it just feels like there is so much happening in the ecosystem and things are moving faster and faster.
zh: 因为感觉这个生态系统里有太多事情在发生,而且事情推进得越来越快。

speaker: Unknown
en: But I think that also is very exciting.
zh: 但我认为这也非常令人兴奋。

speaker: Unknown
en: It's a dynamic time.
zh: 这是一个充满活力的时代。

speaker: Unknown
en: I was gonna say a black swan every quarter or maybe black swan every week.
zh: 我正想说每个季度一只黑天鹅,或者也许是每周一只黑天鹅。

speaker: Unknown
en: Like you sort of don't even, you don't even know if it's a black swan until it's already moved on, right?
zh: 就好像你甚至,你甚至要等到它已经过去了才知道它是不是黑天鹅,对吧?

speaker: Unknown
en: Exactly.
zh: 完全正确。

speaker: Unknown
en: You're on the front lines of changing work habits.
zh: 你处在改变工作习惯的第一线。

speaker: Unknown
en: And I find myself wondering a lot if sort of traditional assessments capture the realities of the US labor market in 2026.
zh: 我发现自己经常在想,那些传统的评估方式是否能捕捉到 2026 年美国劳动力市场的现实。

speaker: Unknown
en: Like the most recent monthly jobs report showed 23,000 jobs lost.
zh: 比如最近一次的月度就业报告显示减少了 23,000 个工作岗位。

speaker: Unknown
en: But at the same time, unemployment numbers went down.
zh: 但与此同时,失业率数字却下降了。

speaker: Unknown
en: Also, how do you make sense of this data?
zh: 另外,你如何理解这些数据?

speaker: Unknown
en: How much do you focus on it?
zh: 你在多大程度上关注它?

speaker: Unknown
en: Does it reflect what you see on Upwork?
zh: 它反映你在 Upwork 上看到的情况吗?

speaker: Unknown
en: Yeah, there are a lot of competing dynamics.
zh: 是的,有很多相互冲突的动态。

speaker: Unknown
en: It certainly doesn't tell the whole story.
zh: 它当然不能说明全部情况。

speaker: Unknown
en: We do see kind of consistent with the jobs report data, the labor market is very subdued.
zh: 我们确实看到,与就业报告数据一致的是,劳动力市场非常低迷。

speaker: Unknown
en: It has been for several quarters.
zh: 已经持续好几个季度了。

speaker: Unknown
en: It continues to be sluggish.
zh: 并且继续保持疲软。

speaker: Unknown
en: I would say we particularly hear about kind of macroeconomic and labor slowdown with our very small business customers.
zh: 我想说的是,我们在非常小的企业客户那里,尤其能听到关于宏观经济和劳动力放缓的声音。

speaker: Unknown
en: You know, those are the guys who are out on the front lines of the economy without a lot of
zh: 你知道,他们是身处经济最前线的人,没有太多

speaker: Unknown
en: Without resourcing, without deep pockets and financial reserves.
zh: 没有资源,没有雄厚的资金和财务储备。

speaker: Unknown
en: And I think they're the ones who are feeling quite pinched right now.
zh: 而我认为,他们正是现在感到相当拮据的群体。

speaker: Unknown
en: And what they tell us is they have pulled back hiring across all channels.
zh: 他们告诉我们,他们已经通过所有渠道缩减了招聘。

speaker: Unknown
en: You guys recently released a future of work index.
zh: 你们最近发布了一份未来工作报告指数。

speaker: Unknown
en: Is that what encapsulates this?
zh: 是这个指数涵盖了这些内容吗?

speaker: Unknown
en: Are there other things in that index that business news headlines maybe aren't capturing?
zh: 这个指数里还有没有其他商业新闻头条可能没有捕捉到的东西?

speaker: Unknown
en: Yeah.
zh: 是的。

speaker: Unknown
en: You know, while the picture overall is of this kind of slow moving market, there are pockets within it that are incredibly vibrant.
zh: 你知道,虽然整体呈现的是这种缓慢运行的市场,但其中有一些极具活力的板块。

speaker: Unknown
en: We really see the growth in...
zh: 我们确实看到了增长在……

speaker: Unknown
en: AI-related skills, AI-related jobs, that is the place where energy and money is flowing.
zh: AI 相关的技能、AI 相关的工作,那是能量和资金正在流入的地方。

speaker: Unknown
en: And we see that in our platform with our own AI category growing over 22% year over year.
zh: 我们在自己的平台上也看到了这一点,我们的 AI 类目同比增长超过 22%。

speaker: Unknown
en: And just all of the data is telling us that the demand from both small businesses all the way up through large enterprises for talent who really know and can help them navigate this new world of work and bring in these relevant skill sets and knowledge of how to use AI tools
zh: 而且所有的数据都在告诉我们,从小企业一直到大型企业,对于真正懂行、能帮助他们驾驭这个新的工作世界、并带来相关技能和 AI 工具使用知识的人才的需求

speaker: Unknown
en: That is really where the energy is going.
zh: 这才是能量真正流向的地方。

speaker: Unknown
en: And the dynamics are moving from full-time towards fractional work, which is a really fascinating trend.
zh: 并且动态正从全职转向零工式工作,这是一个非常引人入胜的趋势。

speaker: Unknown
en: Our most recent survey showed a 10-point increase in freelancing in the U.S. within knowledge workers.
zh: 我们最近的调查显示,美国知识型工作者中的自由职业比例上升了 10 个百分点。

speaker: Unknown
en: It's at 38% of the population today.
zh: 如今占人口的 38%。

speaker: Unknown
en: It was at 28% just a year ago.
zh: 而仅仅一年前还是 28%。

speaker: Unknown
en: So there has been a huge step up in both workers moving into the freelance economy for a variety of reasons, but also businesses saying, you know, we want to find these workers who are out there doing contingent work because we don't necessarily need the same number of full-time employees we needed before.
zh: 所以,无论是出于各种原因进入自由职业经济的劳动者大幅增加,还是企业表示,你知道,我们想找到那些在外从事应急性工作的劳动者,因为我们不再一定需要以前那么多的全职员工。

speaker: Unknown
en: We can approach this work differently, and also we can't access these folks maybe through kind of full-time employment channels.
zh: 我们可以用不同的方式来完成这些工作,而且我们也可能无法通过全职雇佣渠道接触到这些人。

speaker: Unknown
en: There's so much talk about AI potentially taking jobs, and there are some layoffs that companies attribute to AI, and yet you have other CEOs claim that AI is allowing them to add staffing because each AI-enabled person is more productive.
zh: 关于 AI 可能抢走工作的讨论非常多,也有一些公司把裁员归因于 AI,但同时也有其他 CEO 声称 AI 使他们能够增加人员配置,因为每个被 AI 赋能的人生产效率更高。

speaker: Unknown
en: It sounds like both fit in what you're seeing, but it seems early to know what AI's impact is going to be.
zh: 听起来你看到的现象两者都符合,但要弄清 AI 的影响究竟会是什么似乎还为时过早。

speaker: Unknown
en: Or is there something clearer that you see through all of this?
zh: 还是说,你透过这一切看到了某种更清晰的东西?

speaker: Unknown
en: You know, I think it's 60% of jobs that exist today did not exist in 1940.
zh: 你知道,我认为如今存在的 60% 的工作在 1940 年时并不存在。

speaker: Unknown
en: And I think that's helpful context for us as we look at what's happening with AI.
zh: 我认为这对我们审视 AI 正在带来的变化是有帮助的背景。

speaker: Unknown
en: Technology and other forces have, you know, destroyed and created jobs again and again through so many cycles.
zh: 技术和其他力量,你知道,在如此多的周期中一次又一次地摧毁和创造工作。

speaker: Unknown
en: This is kind of a version of that, but happening just bigger and faster, more destructive on the negatives, but also more creative on the positives.
zh: 这有点像是那类情况的一个版本,只是规模更大、速度更快,负面上的破坏性更强,但正面上的创造性也更强。

speaker: Unknown
en: It's a very binary picture.
zh: 这是一幅非常二元对立的画面。

speaker: Unknown
en: You know, there's the camp of
zh: 你知道,有一个阵营认为

speaker: Unknown
en: AI is going to take all the jobs and, you know, humans and the companies, you know, that serve humans and do human solutions are doomed.
zh: AI 将夺走所有的工作,你知道,人类以及服务人类、提供人类解决方案的公司注定完蛋。

speaker: Unknown
en: And then there's the other side.
zh: 然后还有另一面。

speaker: Unknown
en: The reality has to be somewhere in the middle.
zh: 现实必然处于两者之间的某个地方。

speaker: Unknown
en: We do not see mass job destruction as the future.
zh: 我们并不认为大规模的工作毁灭是未来。

speaker: Unknown
en: There is really, I think, a balance to be struck.
zh: 我认为,确实存在一种需要达成的平衡。

speaker: Unknown
en: And, you know, again, there's creation and destruction, but at the end of the day, it's not all destruction.
zh: 而且,你知道,再说一次,有创造也有毁灭,但归根结底,并不全是毁灭。

speaker: Unknown
en: It actually is a lot of new jobs and roles and businesses that are being born because of this exciting technology.
zh: 事实上,正是因为这项令人兴奋的技术,大量的新工作、新角色和新企业正在诞生。

speaker: Unknown
en: You announced in May that you had to cut a quarter of Upwork's corporate staff yourselves.
zh: 你在 5 月宣布,你们自己不得不裁减 Upwork 公司员工的三分之一(四分之一)。

speaker: Unknown
en: You published a pretty frank statement about owning the decision, and you talked about AI but didn't blame AI.
zh: 你发表了一份相当坦率的声明,表示对这个决定负责,你谈到了 AI,但并没有把责任归咎于 AI。

speaker: Unknown
en: Why was that necessary?
zh: 为什么那是必要的?

speaker: Unknown
en: Yeah, I made that decision earlier this year because we really did see that with the market conditions that were changing, this was the right time for us to expand the profitability of the business, which was already part of our long-term goals.
zh: 是的,我在今年早些时候做出了那个决定,因为我们确实看到,随着市场环境的变化,这正是我们扩大业务盈利能力的合适时机,而这本就是我们长期目标的一部分。

speaker: Unknown
en: At the same time, Bob, we've seen that because work is changing, our own work needs to change.
zh: 与此同时,Bob,我们已经看到,因为工作正在改变,我们自己的工作方式也需要改变。

speaker: Unknown
en: And what we did for that was not, you know, really just automating and replacing work or workers with AI.
zh: 而我们为此所做的,并不是,你知道,真正地用 AI 来自动化并取代工作或工作者。

speaker: Unknown
en: Instead, we looked across the entire business and asked ourselves in every team and every department, what would this look like if we really were doing this function from the ground up today using the best technology and tools that are available?
zh: 相反,我们审视了整个公司,在每一个团队和每一个部门问自己:如果我们今天是利用现有最好的技术和工具,从零开始重新做这项职能,它会是什么样子?

speaker: Unknown
en: We also looked at, you know, newer operating organizational models where we could flatten the teams, get more leverage for managers with broader spans of control, fewer layers in the organization.
zh: 我们还审视了,你知道,更新的运营组织模式,我们可以扁平化团队,通过更宽的管理幅度让管理者获得更多杠杆,减少组织中的层级。

speaker: Unknown
en: You know, some of these things that are kind of evergreen opportunities to refine how we operate.
zh: 你知道,其中一些是那种常青的机会,可以用来改进我们的运营方式。

speaker: Unknown
en: I mean, there are contentions, I guess, that some CEOs do AI washing.
zh: 我是说，我想存在一些争议，就是有些 CEO 会做 AI 洗白。

speaker: Unknown
en: They ascribe to AI the reason why they have to make changes as opposed to owning that maybe they didn't have the right strategy in the first place.
zh: 他们把不得不做出变革的原因归到 AI 头上，而不肯承认也许是一开始他们的策略就不对。

speaker: Unknown
en: But by blaming it on AI, like...
zh: 但通过把锅甩给 AI，就像……

speaker: Unknown
en: They get credit for that.
zh: 他们因此得到好评。

speaker: Unknown
en: Their stock price goes up.
zh: 他们的股价上涨。

speaker: Unknown
en: It's like it's a positive.
zh: 就好像这是件好事。

speaker: Unknown
en: And I wonder whether, as you were thinking about this, you were like, well, do I lean into that part of the messaging?
zh: 所以我很好奇，当你在思考这些问题的时候，你是不是想过，嗯，我要不要顺水推舟地采用那部分话术？

speaker: Unknown
en: Because maybe that helps the story.
zh: 因为也许那能让故事更好讲。

speaker: Unknown
en: You know, it was so important to me that our messaging around this be really true and authentic, because frankly, of course, AI is helping us, and it is a contributor to our efficiency and our productivity.
zh: 我想要把它与一位有价值的人类专家结合起来，他能为这个等式带来更多东西。

speaker: Unknown
en: But that is not the biggest reason, A, that we made the changes, nor the biggest benefit that we were able to get from kind of driving these changes.
zh: 但那既不是我们做出变革的最大原因，也不是我们推动这些变革所获得的最大收益。

speaker: Unknown
en: You know, we're actually seeing the opposite trend in our platform in the sense that the AI washing that you're talking about has been happening, but also a lot of folks are now reconsidering and coming back because they're seeing that the humans they let go actually they still need and the AI can't do all of the things that they hoped that it could do.
zh: 你知道，我们在平台上实际看到的趋势恰恰相反，就是说，你说的那种 AI 洗白确实一直在发生，但同时也有很多人现在正在重新考虑并回流，因为他们发现自己裁掉的人类其实仍然需要，而 AI 无法做到他们希望它能做到的所有事情。

speaker: Unknown
en: A recent survey we did showed that 23% of our own clients have actually already moved work back to humans from AI or are about to do so.
zh: 我们最近做的一项调查显示，我们自己的客户中已有 23% 实际上已经把工作从 AI 移回给人类，或者即将这么做。

speaker: Unknown
en: So I think this pendulum, you know, it will keep swinging.
zh: 所以我认为这个钟摆，你知道，它会继续摆动。

speaker: Unknown
en: When we've actually done testing of clients trying to use agents directly to deliver work products through our platform, the failure rate of agents is incredibly high.
zh: 当我们实际测试让客户尝试直接用智能体通过我们的平台交付工作成果时，智能体的失败率高得惊人。

speaker: Unknown
en: They almost never succeed in delivering even fairly simple tasks from clients end to end.
zh: 它们几乎从来没有成功端到端地交付过哪怕是相当简单的客户任务。

speaker: Unknown
en: But when you just add a little bit of human expertise and a few back and forth with an expert, suddenly the success rate goes up more than 70%.
zh: 但只要你加入一点点人类专业知识，与专家进行几轮来回沟通，成功率一下子就提高了 70% 以上。

speaker: Unknown
en: We have to sharpen our intuition around when to trust AI.
zh: 我们必须磨砺自己对何时该信任 AI 的直觉。

speaker: Unknown
en: And I think increasingly people are realizing, ah, I'm not going to take this at face value.
zh: 而且我认为越来越多的人开始意识到，啊，我不会照单全收。

speaker: Unknown
en: I want to couple that with a valued human expert who can bring a lot more to that equation.
zh: 我想把这一点与一位有价值的人类专家结合起来，这位专家能为这个等式带来更多的东西。

speaker: Unknown
en: AI is directly impacting things that happen on your platform.
zh: AI 正在直接影响你的平台上发生的事情。

speaker: Unknown
en: There's been a rise in AI agents.
zh: AI 智能体出现了增长。

speaker: Unknown
en: Posting job ads, machines, essentially trying to hire humans.
zh: 发布招聘广告的机器，本质上是在尝试雇用人类。

speaker: Unknown

speaker: Unknown

speaker: Unknown
en: Now, we're definitely doing this because this is where the world is going already.
zh: 现在，我们这么做确实是因为世界本来就已经朝这个方向发展了。

speaker: Unknown

zh: 这不是我们凭空想出来的东西。

speaker: Unknown

speaker: Unknown
en: And they're having a deliverable that didn't meet expectations or they need a human expert to finish it.

speaker: Unknown

zh: 有了我们的 MCP，现在他们可以直接连接到 Upwork，立即把那个交付成果分享给一位自由职业者，并实时从人类专家那里获得他们需要的按需帮助。

speaker: Unknown

zh: 这是一个巨大的优势，因为现在每个人都期望一切都能实时完成，你知道吗？

speaker: Unknown

zh: 一切都发展得这么快，AI 已经改变了期望，而现在我们也能够满足这种期望，在人们需要额外资源的任何这些 AI 工具内提供真正实时的人类支持。

speaker: Unknown

zh: Upwork 有自己的智能体 Uma，可以协助用户撰写职位描述和准备面试之类的事情。

speaker: Unknown
en: For a platform conceived to give humans more freedom, there's some irony in using AI to prepare a job application so another AI can review it, right?
zh: 对于一个以给人类更多自由为初衷的平台来说，用 AI 去准备一份求职申请、好让另一个 AI 来审阅它，这里面有点讽刺，对吧？

speaker: Unknown
en: Or is it more like, I don't know, like online dating apps where algorithms are better at matching us than we are on our own?
zh: 还是说更像……我也不知道……就像在线交友应用那样，算法比我们自己更擅长给我们做匹配？

speaker: Unknown
en: I mean, these are the big questions and they're the right ones because we are seeing, you know, spam job proposals and applications.
zh: 我是说，这些都是重大的问题，而且也是正确的问题，因为我们确实看到了，你知道，垃圾职位提案和申请。

speaker: Unknown
en: We really just want to put people's own interests and needs on steroids and then have that expressed through the hiring process and the recruitment process that we're supporting them with, including filtering out all of the AI kind of slop and noise that is creeping in now that these tools are so widespread.
zh: 我们真心想要的是把人们自己的兴趣和需求加以强化，然后让他们在我们所支持的招聘流程和招募流程中表达出来，包括过滤掉所有那些随着这些工具泛滥而正在悄悄渗入的 AI 垃圾内容和噪音。

speaker: Unknown
en: Right, I guess because if I'm a job applicant, I guess I can create a lot of different versions of my application to a lot of different jobs that may or may not be right for me and I may not even know what I'm doing.
zh: 对，我想是因为如果我是一名求职者，我可以为很多不同的职位创建我的申请的很多不同版本，而这些职位也许适合我也许不适合，我甚至可能不知道自己在做什么。

speaker: Unknown

zh: 而我想在发布职位的另一端也可能发生同样的事，如果我们能在干草堆里找到那根针，我们就去找，否则我们就只是试试水。

speaker: Unknown

speaker: Unknown
en: It's real data from our platform observing people doing work and delivering for customers with dollars attached.
zh: 这是来自我们平台观察人们实际工作并为客户交付成果的真实数据，并且带有真实的金额。

speaker: Unknown
en: So this is the most verified work history data really in the world, and it's at scale across, you know, 18 million freelancers that were active in the last year.
zh: 所以这是全世界最经过验证的工作履历数据，而且规模覆盖了过去一年活跃的 1800 万名自由职业者。

speaker: Unknown
en: This type of data is what then gives customers confidence in making that hire, not
zh: 正是这类数据让客户有信心做出那次雇用，而不是——

speaker: Unknown

zh: 不是由某个 AI 智能体替他们申请所制造的噪音，也不是那些关于他们专业能力的空洞承诺或声明。

speaker: Unknown
en: It's actually stripping us back to, like, what does the data say in terms of who's good at what?
zh: 它实际上把我们带回到，就像，数据是怎么说的，到底谁擅长什么？

speaker: Unknown
en: And frankly, advancing this meritocratic idea of it shouldn't be about who has the best agent or who sounds the most shiny on paper, but really who has the data and the experience to demonstrate that they can do the work that's required.
zh: 而且坦率地说，它推进了这种精英选拔的理念：不该看谁拥有最好的智能体，或者谁在纸面上听起来最光鲜，而是真正看谁拥有数据和经验来证明他们能完成所需的工作。

speaker: Unknown
en: That in the trenches data Hayden cites illustrates how human in the loop is actually unfolding in an AI world.
zh: Hayden 所引用的这种身处一线的数据，说明了「人在回路」在一个 AI 世界里实际上是如何展开的。

speaker: Unknown

zh: 那里的势头正在积聚并滚雪球式壮大,所以我认为我们采取的方式是为这些工具和我们看到的、已经在显现的这个未来而构建,即使随着事情逐渐成熟和展开,仍然会存在一些持续的波动性。

speaker: Unknown

speaker: Unknown

speaker: Unknown

speaker: Unknown

speaker: Unknown

speaker: Unknown

zh: 而且我认为,很多这些开源模型在合适的控制下是可以安全、可靠地使用的。

zh: 这不是一个二元选择,要么用 Claude,要么就只能自求多福、什么都做不了。

speaker: Unknown

speaker: Unknown

speaker: Unknown
en: I think this is also a place where, for us as a marketplace, creating more of the ecosystem where people can see the pros, the cons, and the costs.
zh: 我认为,这也是对我们这样的市场平台来说,创造更多生态的地方,让人们能看到各种组合的优缺点和成本。

en: of different combinations of AI models or agents with or without human supervision.

zh: 也许我还在业余时间做播客、写书,或者做点创作者经济的事情。

speaker: Unknown
en: And we really have seen this trend towards...
zh: 我们确实看到了这种趋势,即……

speaker: Unknown
en: These portfolio careers.
zh: 这些组合式职业。

speaker: Unknown
en: Gen Z is the biggest one.
zh: Z 世代是最大的一群。

speaker: Unknown
en: 42% of Gen Z are freelancing.
zh: 42% 的 Z 世代在从事自由职业。

speaker: Unknown
en: It's actually them saying, look, I feel more comfortable that I'm not exposed and that I can really both learn and use and build the skills I want and also have income that is predictable and in my control versus at the whim of an employer.
zh: 实际上是他们在说,你看,我觉得更安心,因为我不会把自己暴露在风险中,我可以真正学习和使用、构建我想要的技能,同时拥有可预测、由我自己掌控的收入,而不是任由雇主摆布。

speaker: Unknown
en: It's just a different conception of what a career is for younger folks, right?
zh: 对年轻人来说,这只是对职业的一种不同理解,对吧?

speaker: Unknown
en: Absolutely.
zh: 完全是。

speaker: Unknown
en: And it also reflects, you know, if you think about this AI moment when everyone is trying to prove that they have these skills or if they don't learn them and then prove like, hey, I've gotten these skills now, I'm an AI-relevant employee or worker, freelancing is an amazing way to do that because they're getting on-the-job experience doing real work.
zh: 这也反映出,你知道,想想这个 AI 时刻,每个人都在试图证明自己拥有这些技能,或者如果他们还没学会,就要证明,嘿,我现在已经掌握了这些技能,我是一个与 AI 相关的员工或工作者,自由职业是做到这一点绝佳的方式,因为他们可以获得做实际工作的在职经验。

speaker: Unknown
en: Proving their skills, and if they're on a platform like ours, that comes with a verified work history, all of the marketing kind of around that that freelancers can do to say, hey, now I can earn more and do more.
zh: 证明他们的技能,如果他们在我们这样的平台上,那还附带经过验证的工作履历,以及自由职业者可以围绕它做的各种营销,来说,嘿,现在我可以赚更多、做更多。

speaker: Unknown
en: And we do see them earning more.
zh: 而我们确实看到他们赚得更多。

speaker: Unknown
en: Freelancers that have AI skills are earning 34% more hour.
zh: 拥有 AI 技能的自由职业者每小时收入高出 34%。

speaker: Unknown
en: Than folks who don't have AI skills.
zh: 相比没有 AI 技能的人。

speaker: Unknown
en: And I think that wage gap really speaks to the urgency and the demand from talent to move into a career where maybe in their full-time job they don't have the opportunity to use these tools or they're not learning them inside of their employer.
zh: 而且我认为这个工资差距真正说明了人才的紧迫感和需求,他们想转向一种职业,也许在他们的全职工作中他们没有机会使用这些工具,或者在雇主那里学不到。

speaker: Unknown
en: But here on our platform, they can really demonstrate and flex their muscles around AI and get paid for it.
zh: 但在我们这个平台上,他们可以真正展示和施展他们在 AI 方面的能力,并为此获得报酬。

speaker: Unknown
en: There's a lot of burden on the individual to keep upgrading those skills.
zh: 个人要不断升级这些技能,负担很重。

speaker: Unknown
en: I mean, when software can learn skills way more quickly than humans can, which is what we're seeing with AI, then it does put more pressure on humans, I guess, whether you're in a freelance economy or anywhere, to keep upgrading your own skills or refining your own skills.
zh: 我是说,当软件能比人类快得多地学习技能时——这正是我们在 AI 身上看到的——那确实给人类带来了更多压力,我想,无论你是在自由职业经济中还是其他任何地方,都要不断升级自己的技能或打磨自己的技能。

speaker: Unknown
en: That is the reality, the urgency and the need for all of us.
zh: 这就是现实,是我们所有人的紧迫感和需求。

speaker: Unknown
en: I mean, you, me, all of us to become, you know, fluent in using AI for our jobs.
zh: 我是说,你、我、我们所有人,要变得熟练地在工作中使用 AI。

speaker: Unknown
en: I mean, that is something none of us can escape.
zh: 我是说,这是我们谁都无法逃避的事情。

speaker: Unknown
en: But what we do see is that freelancers, because this actually pays them and puts food on their table, they do it faster.
zh: 但我们确实看到,自由职业者,因为这真正能给他们带来报酬、养家糊口,他们做得更快。

speaker: Unknown
en: They learn faster.
zh: 他们学得更快。

speaker: Unknown
en: They lean in harder.
zh: 他们更积极投入。

speaker: Unknown
en: They move much more quickly to where the new technology is and learning its capabilities and applying those.
zh: 他们更快地转向新技术所在的地方,学习它的能力并应用那些。

speaker: Unknown
en: Capabilities in real work settings.
zh: 在真实的工作场景中应用那些能力。

speaker: Unknown
en: We see this huge advantage actually with the freelance talent pool that's well ahead of full-time employee counterparts in terms of their adoption and facility with AI.
zh: 我们实际上看到自由职业人才库在这方面有巨大优势,在 AI 的采用和熟练程度上远远领先于全职员工同行。

speaker: Unknown
en: And that's another reason why businesses are turning more and more to the freelance economy because they're looking in-house and they're realizing, you know, my team doesn't have these skills and it's going to cost a lot of time and money to try to get my team up a learning curve.
zh: 而这也是企业越来越多地转向自由职业经济的另一个原因,因为他们审视自己的内部,意识到,你知道的,我的团队没有这些技能,而要让我的团队爬上学习曲线要花很多时间和金钱。

speaker: Unknown
en: Maybe I can short circuit that by bringing in freelancers who can both add value and do work.
zh: 也许我可以通过引入自由职业者来走捷径,他们既能增加价值、完成工作。

speaker: Unknown
en: But also upskill my team at the same time as a byproduct of sitting side by side with them.
zh: 又能在与他们并肩工作的过程中,顺带提升我团队的技能。

speaker: Unknown
en: And so there's a lot of that.
zh: 所以有很多这种情况。

speaker: Unknown
en: So it becomes a backdoor way to train my own team at the same time.
zh: 于是这成了一种迂回的方式,同时培训我自己的团队。

speaker: Unknown
en: Exactly.
zh: 没错。

speaker: Unknown
en: And not have to wait for those, you know, fruits to materialize before you start to actually see some real business benefit.
zh: 而且不必等到那些，你知道的，成果真正兑现之后，才开始看到实际的业务收益。

speaker: Unknown
en: Because a freelancer can be adding value in hours.
zh: 因为一个自由职业者可以在几个小时内就开始创造价值。

speaker: Unknown
en: Yeah.
zh: 是的。

speaker: Unknown
en: I mean, well, that is one of the big questions, you know, all of us have is like, how long does it take?
zh: 相反，他们具备演进的能力，能够快速采用并掌握新工具，因为我们知道技术变化得非常快。

speaker: Unknown
en: What's the best way to train people in the AI skills?
zh: 培养人们 AI 技能的最好方式是什么？

speaker: Unknown
en: I was actually talking to one of our clients this morning, and he said, you can't learn to ride a bike in a seminar.
zh: 今天早上我实际上在和我们的一个客户交谈，他说，你不可能在研讨会上学会骑自行车。

speaker: Unknown
en: And I think the same is true for AI.
zh: 我认为对 AI 来说也是一样。

speaker: Unknown
en: You know, you could watch a YouTube tutorial and get more familiar, but at the end of the day, until you're using these tools day in and day out, you know, really integrating and pushing, what's the boundaries of what they can do?
zh: 你知道，你可以看一个 YouTube 教程来变得更加熟悉，但说到底，除非你日复一日地使用这些工具，你知道的，真正地整合并推动，它们能做什么的边界是什么？

speaker: Unknown
en: What are the limitations?
zh: 局限是什么？

speaker: Unknown
en: Why is that?
zh: 为什么会这样？

speaker: Unknown
en: How do I work around that?
zh: 我该如何绕过它？

speaker: Unknown
en: You know, that's when I think people become extremely capable.
zh: 你知道的，我认为当人们做到这些时，才会变得极其能干。

speaker: Unknown
en: And that's one reason we're seeing the rise of a new generalist called the AI Orchestrator.
zh: 而这也是我们看到一种新的通才崛起的原因之一，叫做 AI 编排师。

speaker: Unknown
en: This is becoming extremely popular on our platform because people are looking for someone who can orchestrate and use these AI tools, but also is not necessarily so deep in one domain.
zh: 这在我们的平台上正变得极其流行，因为人们在寻找能够编排并使用这些 AI 工具的人，但也不一定在某个单一领域非常深入。

speaker: Unknown
en: Instead, they have the facility to evolve, adopt new tools, figure them out very quickly because we know the technology is moving so quickly.
zh: 相反，他们拥有进化的能力，能够采用新工具并很快弄明白它们，因为我们知道技术发展得非常快。

speaker: Unknown
en: In what you do as a CEO, how are you using AI?
zh: 作为 CEO，你在工作中是如何使用 AI 的？

speaker: Unknown
en: I think AI, obviously some of its core skills are like data gathering generation and synthesis.
zh: 我认为 AI，显然它的一些核心技能是数据收集、生成和综合。

speaker: Unknown
en: And so inside of our environment, we've set up a very powerful tool, we call it Crystal Ball, and it has access to all of our internal data.
zh: 所以在我们的内部环境中，我们搭建了一个非常强大的工具，我们称之为 Crystal Ball，它可以访问我们所有的内部数据。

speaker: Unknown
en: And this is wonderful for me because instead of having to go ask someone on my team, like, hey, send me the most recent report on this, or like, you know, what happened on this day with this customer type, I can actually just directly query our database just through natural language, get tons of insights around real-time business information, which then we are using in, you know, real-time to make different decisions.
zh: 这对我来说太棒了，因为我不必去找团队里的某个人，比如说，嘿，把关于这个的最新报告发给我，或者，你知道的，某一天这个客户类型发生了什么，我可以直接通过自然语言查询我们的数据库，获得大量关于实时业务信息的洞察，然后我们用这些信息实时做出不同的决策。

speaker: Unknown
en: As I alluded to it at the beginning, you've been CEO through this extraordinary period, you know, pandemic, Ukraine invasion, which prompted you to shut down operations in Russia and Belarus, a backlash against globalization, which also kind of threatens Upwork's premise.
zh: 正如我在开头提到的那样，你在这段非凡的时期里担任 CEO，你知道的，疫情、乌克兰遭入侵，这促使你关闭了在俄罗斯和白俄罗斯的业务，以及对全球化的反弹，这在某种程度上也威胁着 Upwork 的立身之本。

speaker: Unknown
en: One CEO talked to me a while back about building a cadence of change inside his organization to, you know, keep it agile.
zh: 之前有一位 CEO 和我谈到，在他的组织内部建立一种变革的节奏，你知道的，以保持敏捷。

speaker: Unknown
en: But now the cadence of change is like coming from outside.
zh: 但现在变革的节奏像是来自外部。

speaker: Unknown
en: And I wonder how that impacts how you make decisions, how you know what to focus on.
zh: 我想知道这如何影响你做决策的方式，你如何知道该专注于什么。

speaker: Unknown
en: We've worked to try to like remove noise in the organization so that it's very clear the small number of things that we're working on.
zh: 我们一直努力尝试消除组织中的噪音，这样我们正在做的少数几件事就非常清晰。

speaker: Unknown
en: And then if we need to change one of them.
zh: 然后如果我们需要改变其中之一。

speaker: Unknown
en: That we can communicate that really clearly once that decision is made.
zh: 一旦决策做出，我们就能够非常清晰地传达这一点。

speaker: Unknown
en: Because I think, you know, the more cruft there is in the organization around competing priorities and people moving in different directions, that just makes navigating through these types of environments even harder because it's so unstable externally that you need to have, like, full locked down stability and focus internally.
zh: 因为我认为，你知道的，组织中围绕相互竞争的优先级和人们朝不同方向前进的冗余越多，就会让穿越这类环境的导航变得更加困难，因为外部如此不稳定，你需要拥有，比如，内部完全锁定的稳定和专注。

speaker: Unknown
en: We've also changed our planning horizons.
zh: 我们也改变了我们的规划周期。

speaker: Unknown
en: I'd say, you know, in the past, you know, I was a product manager for many years before becoming a CEO.
zh: 我想说，你知道的，在过去，你知道的，在成为 CEO 之前我做了很多年产品经理。

speaker: Unknown
en: And, you know, you would have like a one-year roadmap.
zh: 而且，你知道的，你会有一份一年的路线图。

speaker: Unknown
en: And yeah, like it would change and everything else, but it didn't feel unreasonable to have some idea of what you want to be doing for a full year.
zh: 然后，是的，比如它会发生变化什么的，但对自己整整一年想做什么有一些想法并不觉得不合理。

speaker: Unknown
en: Now in product, if you have a one-year roadmap and really you're executing the same thing in month 11 that you thought you would be, you know, when you started, something's probably wrong because you will have learned so much more and the technology will become more capable.
zh: 现在在产品方面，如果你有一份一年的路线图，而实际上你在第 11 个月执行的还是你，你知道的，开始时所想的同一件事，那可能就有问题了，因为你会学到多得多的东西，技术也会变得更强大。

speaker: Unknown
en: So we've shortened some of our planning cycles, still setting kind of big ambitious goals out in the future, but not being as committal to, you know, the steps required to get there.
zh: 所以我们缩短了一些规划周期，仍然在未来设定远大而有野心的目标，但不再那么执着于，你知道的，达到那里所需的步骤。

speaker: Unknown
en: It's kind of like, let's take the first step and then reevaluate what is that second step?
zh: 这有点像，让我们先迈出第一步，然后重新评估第二步是什么？

speaker: Unknown
en: Let's not presume that from this vantage point today,
zh: 我们不要预设，从今天的这个视角出发，

speaker: Unknown
en: We know what that is.
zh: 我们知道那是什么。

speaker: Unknown
en: And when you're trying to focus and prioritize, like, do you have tools that you use to do that?
zh: 而当你试图专注并排定优先级时，比如，你有用来做这件事的工具吗？

speaker: Unknown
en: I mean, I remember talking to Daniel Eck at Spotify at one point, and he would say each quarter he'd like create a list of 10 things, but they were ranked.
zh: 我是说，我记得有一次和 Spotify 的 Daniel Eck 交谈，他说每个季度他会列一个 10 件事的清单，但它们是有排序的。

speaker: Unknown
en: Like you couldn't go to number two until you satisfied number one.
zh: 比如，在满足第一项之前，你不能去做第二项。

speaker: Unknown
en: We use ranked lists all the time, like Daniel.
zh: 我们一直都在使用排序清单，和 Daniel 一样。

speaker: Unknown
en: I think that's a really important one.
zh: 我认为这是非常重要的一点。

speaker: Unknown
en: We also look at kind of what is our portfolio, how much resource we're putting in for things that we have a really high confidence will deliver in the near to medium term because it's a road we've gone down before and we know it well versus where are we putting resourcing in for things that are much more speculative or building for future states that we anticipate or can kind of see coming but may not have arrived yet.
zh: 我们还会审视我们的组合是什么样的，我们在哪些事情上投入多少资源，这些事情我们非常有信心能在近期到中期交付，因为这是我们以前走过的路，我们很熟悉； versus 我们在哪些地方投入资源于更具投机性的事情，或者为我们预期或能隐约看到但可能尚未到来的未来状态进行构建。

speaker: Unknown
en: And I think it's become even more important in this environment to be very clear and have
zh: 我认为在这种环境下，更加重要的是要非常清晰，并且

speaker: Unknown
en: Internal alignment around how much of each of those activities you're doing.
zh: 在内部就这些活动各自占多少比例达成一致。

speaker: Unknown
en: And also when you make changes, again, maybe something that was out in the future, six months later, now it's here, it's arrived today, you know, it has to move into the other part of the portfolio.
zh: 而且当你做出改变时，再说一次，也许某件原本在未来的事情，六个月之后，现在它到来了，它今天已经到了，你知道的，它必须移入组合的另一部分。

speaker: Unknown
en: And then you've got to be thinking, okay, where are we investing in that next, next horizon once now that we've, you know, accomplished the thing that was out there in front of us.
zh: 然后你就得思考，好，既然我们已经，你知道的，完成了摆在面前的那件事，那么下一个、再下一个地平线我们要投资在哪里。

speaker: Unknown
en: What's at stake for the future of work right now?
zh: 眼下工作的未来面临什么利害关系？

speaker: Unknown
en: The binary debate that's happening around, you know, will humans win or machines win, I think that is distracting us from, in some cases, putting, you know, our collective societal energy towards building a future where everyone wins, where humans win with AI and empowered by AI, but not at the loss, you know, of jobs, opportunities, and purpose that people, you know, have and will, I think, always need from doing meaningful work.
zh: 围绕着，你知道的，人类会赢还是机器会赢而正在发生的二元辩论，我认为这让我们分心，在某些情况下，没有把我们，你知道的，集体的社会能量投入到建设一个人人皆赢的未来，人类借助 AI 并被 AI 赋能而获胜，但不是以牺牲，你知道的，工作、机会和意义感为代价，这些是人们，你知道的，已经拥有而且我认为永远需要从有意义的工作中获得的。

speaker: Unknown
en: Well, Hayden, this was great.
zh: 好的，Hayden，这次对话非常棒。

speaker: Unknown
en: Thanks so much for doing it.
zh: 非常感谢你来参加。

speaker: Unknown
en: Thank you so much.
zh: 非常感谢。

speaker: Unknown
en: Great to see you.
zh: 很高兴见到你。

speaker: Unknown
en: There's so many rich insights in Hayden's comments about how to lead in changing environments, about the good and bad of AI agents, about how to build skills today, and Gen Z's changing perspective on work and careers.
zh: Hayden 的谈话中有许多深刻的见解，涉及如何在变化的环境中领导、AI 智能体的好与坏、如今如何培养技能，以及 Z 世代对工作和职业不断变化的看法。

speaker: Unknown
en: I keep coming back to her reflection on meritocracy, that Upwork's system quantifies and captures what specific human talent actually gets done and the value delivered.
zh: 我不断回想起她关于精英体制的反思，即 Upwork 的系统量化并记录了具体的人才实际完成了什么工作，以及所交付的价值。

speaker: Unknown
en: When it comes to how AI will change the future of work, so much of the data is essentially guesswork.
zh: 至于 AI 将如何改变未来的工作，大部分数据本质上都是猜测。

speaker: Unknown
en: Of course, gazing into the future has always entailed a bunch of guesswork.
zh: 当然，展望未来从来都伴随着大量猜测。

speaker: Unknown
en: Whatever crystal ball Upwork has built internally, it only reflects the past.
zh: 无论 Upwork 内部构建了什么样的水晶球，它都只反映过去。

speaker: Unknown
en: But what we do know is that what's valuable to humans can only be determined by humans.
zh: 但我们知道的是，对人类而言什么是有价值的，只能由人类来决定。

speaker: Unknown
en: Appreciating what we each do and how we do it, that's something that will always stand the test of time.
zh: 欣赏我们每个人做了什么以及如何做的，这是永远经得起时间考验的东西。

zh: 我是 Bob Safian。

speaker: Unknown
en: Thanks for listening.
zh: 感谢收听。

en: Humans will never be more intelligent than AI.
zh: 人类的智能永远不会超过 AI。

speaker: Unknown
en: There's going to be two types of companies.
zh: 未来将会有两种类型的公司。

speaker: Unknown
en: Those are great at AI and those that went out of business because they weren't.
zh: 一种是擅长 AI 的，另一种是因为不擅长而倒闭的。

en: How do we build a future that is human-centered?
zh: 我们如何构建一个以人为中心的未来？

zh: 我是 Rana Elkayubi,在我的播客 Pioneers of AI 中，我们回答这个问题以及更多其他问题。

zh: 作为一名 AI 科学家、创业者和投资人，我知道构建对每个人都有效的 AI 需要什么。

en: Every week, I sit down with the pioneers shaping our future, and we take you behind the scenes of the AI that's transforming our lives.
zh: 每周，我都会与塑造我们未来的先驱者们坐下来交谈，带你走进正在改变我们生活的 AI 的幕后。
